rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The body is an instrument for the soul to acquire true knowledge and virtue; dying without either leaves profound regret over wasting a means to eternal happiness.
rows.anchor: { ولقد جئتمونا فرادى كما خلقناكم أول مرة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People invert their proper journey from bodily life toward the spiritual world by pursuing wealth and status; at death their possessions remain useless behind them, intensifying regret.
rows.anchor: والإنسان في الحقيقة متوجه من العالم الجسماني إلى العالم الروحاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth used for no good purpose is left behind, but wealth spent to honor God and show compassion to creation is sent ahead, as 2:110 says.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى : { وما تقدموا لانفسكم من خير تجدوه عند الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who labored for false religions expecting aid at the Resurrection instead encounter their doctrines’ severe, lasting punishment and the absence of their supposed partners.
rows.anchor: وما نرى معكم شفعاءكم الذين زعمتم أنهم فيكم شركاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment includes regret for hardship spent gaining only torment, shame at recognizing their worldly beliefs as error, and despair after intense hope.
rows.anchor: منها عذاب الحسرة والندامة : وهو أنه كيف أنفق ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once certainty makes recovery impossible, grief becomes acute; the severed connection between soul and body cannot be restored.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أن الوصلة الحاصلة بين النفس والجسد قد تقطعت ولا سبيل إلى تحصيلها مرة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After threatening the nations, God encourages them by recalling His favors: provision and settlement on earth, then Adam’s creation and honor; a favor to their forefather benefits his descendants.
rows.anchor: ثم أتبعه بذكر أنه خلق أبانا آدم وجعله مسجودا للملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This repeats the reasoning of 2:28: God forbids disobedience by recalling life after death and His many favors, including earthly benefits and Adam’s honor, so rebellion and ingratitude are unfitting.
rows.anchor: وعلل ذلك المنع بكثرة نعمه على الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Adam and Iblis narrative appears in seven Qur’anic locations: al-Baqara, al-Aʿraf, al-Hijr, Bani Israʾil, al-Kahf, Ta-Ha, and Sad.
rows.anchor: ذكر قصة آدم عليه السلام مع قصة إبليس في القرآن في سبعة مواضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi raises a chronological problem: the address seems to mean current humanity was created and formed before God then commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam.
rows.anchor: يفيد أن المخاطب بهذا الخطاب نحن

rows.speaker: الحسن ويوسف النخوي
rows.claim: They take “created and formed you” to mean Adam, resolving the sequence because the command to prostrate followed Adam’s creation; Razi calls this the chosen view.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الحسن ويوسف النخوي وهو المختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The collective address can refer to Adam because he is humanity’s origin, as scripture and ordinary speech address descendants or a group through their ancestor or one member.
rows.anchor: إن آدم عليه السلام أصل البشر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says God created Adam, formed Adam’s descendants as particles in his loins, and only then commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول مجاهد . فذكر أنه تعالى خلق آدم أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading makes the sequence order statements rather than events: after creating and forming humanity, God tells them that He had commanded the angels to prostrate.
rows.anchor: فهذا العطف يفيد ترتيب خبر على خبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fourth interpretation takes creation linguistically as determination: “We created you” refers to God’s decree and will to bring human beings into this world.
rows.anchor: أن الخلق في اللغة عبارة عن التقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We formed you” refers to God recording in the Preserved Tablet the forms of all beings destined to exist until the Resurrection, before actual creation of Adam.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أنه تعالى أثبت في اللوح المحفوظ صورة كل شيء كائن محدث إلى قيام الساعة

words: خلقناكم ثم صورناكم ثم قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, after decree and inscription God actually created Adam and ordered the angels to prostrate; Razi judges it closer than the other explanations.
rows.anchor: ثم بعد هذين الأمرين أحدث الله تعالى آدم وأمر الملائكة بالسجود له وهذا التأويل عندي أقرب من سائر الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One previously discussed view holds that prostration itself was only an act of reverence, without making Adam the one prostrated to.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أن المراد منها مجرد التعظيم لانفس السجدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view says the prostration was to God, with Adam serving as the direction or qibla.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : أن المراد هو السجدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view holds that Adam himself was the one prostrated to.
rows.anchor: أن المسجود له هو آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars dispute whether the commanded angels were the angels of the heavens and Throne or the angels of the earth.
rows.anchor: اختلفوا في أن الملائكة الذين أمرهم الله تعالى بالسجود لآدم هل هم ملائكة السموات والعرش أو المراد ملائكة الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent exception makes Iblis seem to be one of the angels, though Razi refers to earlier arguments against that conclusion.
rows.anchor: ظاهر الآية يدل على أنه تعالى استثنى إبليس من الملائكة ، فوجب كونه منهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan denies that Iblis was an angel: he was made of fire, whereas angels are of light and do not disobey, become arrogant, or grow weary.
rows.anchor: وكان الحسن يقول : إبليس لم يكن من الملائكة لأنه خلق من نار والملائكة من نور

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan distinguishes Iblis as a jinn, whereas angels are neither jinn nor merely beings outside God’s messengers.
rows.anchor: وكان الحسن يقول : إبليس لم يكن من الملائكة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan calls Iblis the first jinn and their father, paralleling Adam as the first human and father of humanity.
rows.anchor: وكان الحسن يقول : إبليس لم يكن من الملائكة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Iblis had another name, was a believing worshipper in heaven, and was called Iblis after disobeying and being sent down.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : ولما كان إبليس مأمورا مع الملائكة استثناه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to prostrate included Iblis, apparently implying he was an angel, although Razi says the earlier proofs establish otherwise and the exception was addressed under al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: فإن ذلك الأمر قد تناول إبليس

rows.speaker: الكسائي والفراء والزجاج والأكثرون
rows.claim: The popular grammatical view treats la as extra, yielding “What prevented you from prostrating?”; al-Kisaʾi, al-Farraʾ, al-Zajjaj, and most scholars hold this.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الكسائي ، والفراء ، والزجاج ، والأكثرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers that la carries meaning, since declaring a word in God’s Book useless is difficult and problematic.
rows.anchor: ههنا مفيدة وليست لغوا وهذا هو الصحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One meaningful reading asks what stopped Iblis from refraining from prostration, as an accusatory rhetorical question implying that no such restraint existed.
rows.anchor: ويكون هذا الاستفهام على سبيل الإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The analogy is a question to someone who unjustly struck the speaker: what prevented him—religion, reason, or shame?—implying none did.
rows.anchor: كقول القائل لمن ضربه ظلما : ما

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi reads “prevented” as “prompted”: God asks what induced Iblis not to prostrate, since defying God’s command is astonishing.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : ذكر الله المنع وأراد الداعي

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Scholars infer that a command form entails obligation because God blamed Iblis for leaving what He had commanded.
rows.anchor: احتج العلماء بهذه الآية على أن صيغة الأمر تفيد الوجوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “when I commanded you” explains the blame by the command simply as a command, not a special instance; therefore every command entails obligation.
rows.anchor: هو الأمر من حيث أنه أمر لا كونه أمرا مخصوصا

rows.speaker: المحتجون بأن الأمر يفيد الفور
rows.claim: Those who say commands require immediate performance argue that Iblis was blamed for failing to prostrate at once; otherwise immediate delay would not warrant blame.
rows.anchor: ذم إبليس على ترك السجود في الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis says he refused because he considered himself superior and believed a superior being should not be ordered to serve an inferior; fire, he argues, is better than clay.
rows.anchor: ومن كان خيرا من غيره فإنه لا يجوز أمر ذلك الأكمل بالسجود لذلك الأدون

words: خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis’s case ranks fire above clay as celestial, subtle, light, and active, while clay is dark, low, dense, heavy, and receptive; it associates fire with life and earthiness with death.
rows.anchor: والأرض ليس لها إلا القبول والانفعال . والفعل أشرف من الانفعال

words: خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also appeals to heat’s role in ripening fruit and growth, contrasting it with cold, dry old age, which he calls the worst period of human life.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فنضج الثمار متعلق بالحرارة

words: خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects the premise that superior material makes a superior form: virtue is a gift from God, so a better origin does not guarantee a better creature.
rows.anchor: لما كانت الفضيلة عطية من الله ابتداء لم يلزم من فضيلة المادة فضيلة الصورة

words: خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings a disbeliever from a believer and a believer from a disbeliever, and light from darkness and vice versa; virtue therefore comes from God, not the original substance.
rows.anchor: وذلك يدل على أن الفضيلة لا تحصل إلا بفضل الله تعالى لا بسبب فضيلة الأصل والجوهر

words: خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moral responsibility concerns the living person after reaching mature reason, so evaluation depends on what the person becomes, not the material from which he was made.
rows.anchor: فالمعتبر بما انتهى إليه لا بما خلق منه

words: خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Merit comes from deeds rather than material origin: a believing Abyssinian is better than an unbelieving Qurayshi.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فالفضل إنما يكون بالأعمال وما يتصل بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis’s further premise is that it is rationally indecent to command a superior to serve an inferior; Razi illustrates it with leading jurists ordered to serve a lesser jurist.
rows.anchor: أن من أمر أبا حنيفة والشافعي وسائر أكابر الفقهاء بخدمة فقيه نازل الدرجة كان ذلك قبيحا في العقول

rows.speaker: المحتجون بمنع تخصيص العموم بالقياس
rows.claim: Opponents of specifying general scripture by analogy argue that the general command included Iblis, who exempted himself through a fire-over-clay analogy; his severe blame shows such specification is impermissible.
rows.anchor: احتج من قال : أنه لا يجوز تخصيص عموم النص بالقياس

words: فما يكون لك أن تتكبر فيها
rows.speaker: المحتجون بمنع تخصيص العموم بالقياس
rows.claim: They add that God calls Iblis arrogant after his analogical exception, making attempts to qualify a general divine text through analogy an act of arrogance toward God.
rows.anchor: وهذا يقتضي أن من حاول تخصيص عموم النص بالقياس تكبر على الله

words: فما يكون لك أن تتكبر فيها
rows.speaker: المحتجون بمنع تخصيص العموم بالقياس
rows.claim: Since arrogance toward God brings severe punishment and expulsion from the elect into the ranks of the accursed, the argument concludes that analogy cannot specify general scripture.
rows.anchor: التكبر على الله يوجب العقاب الشديد والإخراج من زمرة الأولياء والإدخال في زمرة الملعونين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi reports Ibn Abbas saying obedience was preferable to analogy for Iblis: he disobeyed and analogized, became the first to analogize and disbelieved, and God joins self-directed religious analogizers with him.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس أنه قال : كانت الطاعة أولى بإبليس من القياس

rows.speaker: المعترضون
rows.claim: An objection distinguishes analogy that cancels a text entirely, which is invalid, from analogy that only specifies some cases, whose invalidity still needs proof.
rows.anchor: القياس الذي يبطل النص بالكلية باطل . أما القياس الذي يخصص النص في بعض الصور

rows.speaker: المعترضون
rows.claim: The objector argues that if fire-born Iblis could not be ordered to bow to earth-born Adam, then light-born angels would have an even stronger exemption, nullifying the command altogether.
rows.anchor: لكان قبح أمر من كان مخلوقا من النور المحض بالسجود لمن كان مخلوقا من الأرض أولى وأقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that service is objectionable only when the superior refuses it: angels willingly surrendered that right, but Iblis did not; the analogy would specify rather than erase the text, yet Iblis’s blame shows specification is forbidden.
rows.anchor: أما الملائكة فقد رضوا بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God asks why Iblis did not prostrate; Iblis answers that he was made from fire and Adam from clay; God then orders Iblis to descend.
rows.anchor: لا شك أن قائل هذا القول هو الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi asks why Iblis received direct divine speech if such speech honors Moses; if it does not confer honor, why does scripture present God’s speech to Moses as a great distinction?
rows.anchor: فإن كانت هذه المكالمة تفيد الشرف العظيم فكيف حصلت على أعظم الوجوه لإبليس

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars say God addressed Iblis through an angelic intermediary, since they hold that God speaks to non-prophets only through a mediator.
rows.anchor: أن بعض العلماء قال : إنه تعالى قال لإبليس

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Other scholars accept direct speech to Iblis but treat it as humiliation; God’s speech to Moses and other prophets was honor, as shown by His words to Moses.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قال : إنه تعالى تكلم مع إبليس بلا واسطة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says “descend from it” means descend from the Garden, which was the Garden of Eden where Adam was created.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد من الجنة

rows.speaker: بعض المعتزلة
rows.claim: Some Muʿtazilites say Iblis was ordered to descend from heaven.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المعتزلة : أنه إنما أمر بالهبوط من السماء

words: فما يكون لك أن تتكبر فيها
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas takes “therein” as heaven, whose angelic inhabitants are humble and reverent.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد أن أهل السموات ملائكة متواضعون خاشعون

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj glosses “the abased” as humiliation; God subjected Iblis to abasement because he sought arrogance.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : إن إبليس طلب التكبر فابتلاه الله تعالى بالذلة والصغار

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Razi invokes the Prophet’s saying that whoever humbles himself for God is raised by God, while whoever acts arrogantly is brought low.
rows.anchor: من تواضع لله رفعه الله ومن تكبر وضعه الله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another explanation says that when Iblis displayed arrogance, God clothed him in humiliation.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لما أظهر الاستكبار ألبس الصغار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi lists ten issues deferred to al-Baqara: whether dwelling is worship or permission, Eve’s creation, the garden’s location, eating as permission, prohibition as disapproval or ban, tree identity and kind, sin severity, injustice and condemnation, and whether this preceded Adam’s prophethood.
rows.anchor: فهذه المسائل العشرة قد سبق تفصيلها وتقريرها في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining difference from 2:35 is waw there versus fa here: waw gives conjunction generally, while fa adds succession, so succession is a subtype of conjunction.
rows.anchor: أن الواو تفيد الجمع المطلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi resolves the wording difference by saying al-Baqara gives the general category, while al-Aʿraf specifies the particular kind of conjunction.
rows.anchor: ففي سورة البقرة ذكر الجنس وفي سورة الأعراف ذكر النوع
